deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a 'système de pseudo-droites' Σ=(X,Σ) is an arrangement of pseudolines D_i in a topological projective plane X. Its 1-skeleton is a combinatorial map ('carte') C, with dual C*. In the 1983-84 notes this C is studied through the cartographic formalism of the Esquisse period.

Part 1 (top left). This continues an argument from the previous page, so the setting is only partly visible.
- A combined map built from C and C* (written 'C C') is used. Its faces are read off locally.
- The edges of a face biject with the edges of the local polygon of the edges issuing from a vertex σ, or equivalently with the vertices of Γ incident to that face.
- More precisely, the combinatorial polygon attached to such a face, viewed as a boundary, is canonically isomorphic to the dual of the combinatorial polygon of the corresponding face of C C.
- In the case of interest (coming from a pseudoline system in the relevant position), the order of these faces is (a divisor of) 4. This is consistent with 4-valent crossings or with the quadrangular faces of a vertex-face (radial) construction.
- Among the faces along a boundary component, which corresponds to a cycle of the map C, one is 'privileged'.

Part 2 (top right). The 'type' property that singles out the privileged face does not, in general, depend only on the incident vertices of C. It depends on the particular edges considered. Hence one cannot hope, in general, to realise C as the union of two conjugate graphs γ, γ* (each a map realised in the faces of the other, like a graph and its dual in a Tait/medial-type decomposition).
A modern gloss consistent with this: in RP², the 4-valent arrangement map is face-2-colourable iff the number of pseudolines is even. A non-contractible loop crosses every pseudoline an odd number of times. So a checkerboard-type splitting is not available in general.

Part 3 (bottom right), a new start. Fix a pseudoline L.
- A narrow tubular neighbourhood β_L of L is a Möbius band.
- Its boundary L̃ is a connected double cover of L (the 'revêtement des rives', the two banks).
- The complement Δ_L of the open band is a closed disk.
- Every other D_i ∈ Σ meets ∂Δ_L = L̃ in exactly two points (the two banks over the point D_i∩L). Its trace on Δ_L is a segment, as is its trace on β_L.
- So Σ minus L becomes a 'système de cordes' in the disk Δ_L. This is the disk/chord model of the affine arrangement obtained by sending L to infinity.
- The next page characterises such chord systems combinatorially: pairwise crossing at most once, parallel classes, and endpoints in antipodal blocks. It then introduces 'arcs de généralisation/spécialisation' via the boundary triangles.

Purpose: a combinatorial (map-theoretic) classification of pseudoline arrangements, and of their behaviour under choice of a line at infinity, presumably towards moduli/'généralisation–spécialisation' of arrangements.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible. The statement 'the order of the faces is (a divisor of) 4' is under-specified on this page. It depends on the definition of the combined map 'C C' from the previous page, which is not visible, and cannot be checked here.
The claim that the distinguished 'type' depends on edges and not only vertices is asserted, not proved. It is plausible, given non-orientability and parity obstructions in RP².

ideas.what: The tubular neighbourhood of a pseudoline in the projective plane is a Möbius band. Its boundary is the connected double cover (two 'rives') and its complement is a disk.
ideas.modern_name: Möbius band / disk decomposition of RP² along a pseudoline
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical topology; used in pseudoline theory by Levi (1926), Ringel (1956), Grünbaum, Goodman–Pollack

ideas.what: Removing L turns the arrangement into a system of chords in a disk, each chord meeting the boundary in two points; the realisable chord systems are characterised combinatorially (continued on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: affine pseudoline arrangement / disk (chord, wiring-diagram) model; allowable sequences

ideas.what: Treating the arrangement as a combinatorial map C with its dual C*, comparing face polygons via canonical duality, and noting that faces have order dividing 4.
ideas.modern_name: medial/radial map of an arrangement; cartographic-group description of maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: map theory (Tutte; Jones–Singerman 1978); Grothendieck's 'cartes' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions pseudoline systems ('systèmes de pseudo-droites') and maps only in passing

ideas.what: Obstruction: the arrangement map cannot in general be realised as the union of two mutually dual ('conjugate') graphs γ, γ*, because the privileged face type depends on edges and not only on vertices.
ideas.modern_name: failure of Tait/checkerboard (graph–dual) decomposition in RP² (parity of the number of lines)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in arrangement and knot-diagram theory

missed.claim: Historical: Grothendieck developed a map-theoretic ('cartes', dual maps, conjugate graphs) approach to pseudoline arrangements in 1983-84, contemporaneous with Goodman–Pollack. This interest is barely mentioned (only allusively in the Esquisse) and is essentially absent from the arrangement literature.
missed.quote: il n'y a pas question d'espérer, en général, de réaliser C comme réunion de deux graphes γ, γ*, correspondants à deux cartes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents a link between the dessins/cartographic programme and oriented-matroid/pseudoline combinatorics that the later literature did not develop. The mathematics on this page itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard pseudoline topology (Möbius band, disk complement, chord model) plus a local map-duality remark. The only interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck framing arrangements in his map/dessin language.
transcription_corrections: 'Donc il y a pas question' should read 'Donc il n'y a pas question'.
'(rev. des rives)' = '(revêtement des rives)', i.e. L̃ is the double cover formed by the two banks of the band.
'l'ordre des faces ces faces' is a duplicated phrase; read 'l'ordre de ces faces'.
'et L ... une position relative' is likely a misreading. Context requires L to be a pseudoline (possibly 'L ∈ Σ' or 'L une pseudo-droite'), with the inserted '(de Möbius)' qualifying the band β_L.
'toutes en position relative' is uncertain; it may be 'en position générale/relative' in a specific sense defined earlier.
The struck word before 'graphes γ, γ*' is 'cartes C, C' (crossed out), and the insertion reads roughly 'cartes réalisées par'.
